RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Member: Cameron Brooks
Member ID: W295648415
Reference Number: POC-0948834B99-90261
Date of Notice: 2026-08-25
Requested Service: Cervical fusion (ACDF), CPT 22551
Ordering Surgeon: Marchetti, MD, Orthopedic Surgery

To the Grievance and Appeals Review Team:

I am writing to appeal the denial of prior authorization for anterior cervical discectomy and fusion (ACDF), CPT 22551, communicated in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-25 (Reference No. POC-0948834B99-90261). This appeal is submitted within the 180-day deadline stated in that notice (by 2027-02-21).

Stated Reason for Denial

The notice states that the request was denied because "the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery." I respectfully disagree and ask that the plan reconsider this determination based on the clinical record summarized below, which I believe was not adequately reflected in the initial review.

Applicable Medical Necessity Criteria

Based on our research, Anthem's coverage determinations for cervical spine surgery in Kentucky are made using the Carelon Medical Benefits Management (formerly AIM Specialty Health) "Spine Surgery" Clinical Appropriateness Guideline (Doc ID MSK03-1125.1-UC0126), the version effective 2025-11-15 (codes updated 2026-01-01), available at https://guidelines.carelonmedicalbenefitsmanagement.com/spine-surgery-2025-11-15-updated-2026-01-01/. I have not received formal written confirmation from Anthem that this specific document and version were the ones applied to my request, and I ask the plan to confirm this in its appeal response or to identify the specific policy actually used if different.

Subject to that confirmation, the guideline text we were able to retrieve for the "Cervical Decompression With or Without Fusion" section states:

"When imaging studies demonstrate nerve root compression due to herniated disc or spondylotic osteophyte correlating with the distribution of signs and symptoms, and ANY of the following criteria apply: Objective neurologic findings which correlate with a cervical nerve root impingement · Progressive or severe neurologic deficits secondary to spinal cord or foraminal compression · Unremitting radicular pain which has not responded to at least 6 weeks of appropriate conservative management (physical therapy optional)"

Everything beyond the quoted passage above is our own summary or argument, not plan language, because we were not able to retrieve additional sections (such as the exclusions list) of the guideline in full.

How the Clinical Record Satisfies This Criterion

The documentation submitted with the prior authorization request satisfies this criterion in more than one independent way:

1. Imaging correlating with distribution of signs and symptoms: MRI of the cervical spine dated 2026-06-29 demonstrates a C5-C6 disc herniation with severe right foraminal narrowing and C6 nerve root compression. This correlates directly with the patient's reported radicular pain and numbness into the right thumb and index finger — the classic C6 dermatomal distribution — and with weakness on exam.

2. Objective neurologic findings which correlate with a cervical nerve root impingement: Physical examination documented positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level (C6), together with weakness in the right thumb/index finger distribution.

3. Unremitting radicular pain which has not responded to at least 6 weeks of appropriate conservative management: The record documents:
   - 14 months of progressive neck pain unrelieved by rest;
   - 8 weeks (18 visits) of supervised physical therapy, including cervical traction and postural training, from 2026-05-03 to 2026-06-28, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note;
   - 4 months of NSAID therapy with inadequate relief;
   - A corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-05 that produced only 2 weeks of partial relief.

This 8-week course of supervised physical therapy, combined with 4 months of NSAID therapy and a corticosteroid injection, exceeds the "at least 6 weeks of appropriate conservative management" referenced in the guideline language quoted above, and the record shows this conservative treatment did not durably resolve the patient's radicular pain. In addition, because the guideline criterion is satisfied by "ANY" of the three listed findings, the objective neurologic findings and correlating imaging described above independently support medical necessity even apart from the conservative-treatment history.

Additional Relevant Facts

- No active infection is documented.
- No untreated substance use is documented.
- BMI is 29, and the patient is a non-smoker, with no documented contraindications to surgery.

Requested Action

Based on the clinical documentation summarized above, I ask that Anthem reverse the denial and approve prior authorization for CPT 22551 (ACDF) as requested by Dr. Marchetti. If the plan applied a different medical policy or guideline version than the one identified above, I ask that Anthem specify that document by name, number, and effective date, and identify the specific criterion or criteria it found unmet, so that this appeal (or a further appeal) can directly address it.

Enclosed / Available Upon Request

- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-05-03 to 2026-06-28, 18 visits)
- Medication and injection records (NSAID trial; corticosteroid injection 2026-05-05)
- MRI cervical spine report dated 2026-06-29
- Clinic notes documenting exam findings, provocative testing, and neurologic deficit
- Surgeon's letter of medical necessity from Dr. Marchetti [if available/enclosed]

Please confirm receipt of this appeal and advise of the timeframe for a written decision. If this matter qualifies for expedited review due to the patient's ongoing pain, numbness, and weakness, please advise how to request expedited handling. If the internal appeal is not resolved in the patient's favor, I understand I may have the right to request an independent external review under applicable Kentucky and federal law (45 CFR §147.136), and I ask that Anthem include instructions for that process with its response.
